title: Wings Over the Atlantic
tagline: The skies were closed to women — until she flew through them.

scenes.text: Newfoundland, May 20, 1932. A red Lockheed Vega sits on Harbour Grace airfield. The pilot climbs in alone — no navigator, minimal radio. Amelia Earhart intends to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean. No woman has done it before. Tonight she follows Lindbergh's path — alone.

scenes.speaker: Amelia Earhart
scenes.text: Women must try to do things as men have tried. When they fail, their failure must be but a challenge to others. The most difficult thing is the decision to act. The rest is merely tenacity.

challenge.fact: Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan disappeared on July 2, 1937, near tiny Howland Island in the Central Pacific — one of the most remote spots on Earth. They were never found. Her disappearance remains one of aviation's great mysteries.
challenge.instruction: Amelia Earhart disappeared near which island during her 1937 round-the-world attempt? Order the grid as the record was ordered — every row, column and box complete.

scenes.text: The flight was harrowing. Ice formed on the wings and caused a spin. Her altimeter broke. Fire broke out near the exhaust manifold. She flew through storms for 14 hours and 56 minutes — and landed in a field in Northern Ireland.

scenes.speaker: Amelia Earhart
scenes.text: A farmer walked up to my plane. He said, 'Have you come far?' I said, 'From America.' The look on his face was worth everything.

challenge.instruction: Chart Earhart's course through the storm corridors over the Atlantic.
challenge.fact: In 1932, Earhart flew solo from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland in 14 hours 56 minutes — battling icing, storm turbulence, and a leaking fuel tank.

challenge.instruction: Earth's orbit is an ellipse. Earhart circled the globe — calculate the area of the elliptical flight path around the equator.
challenge.fact: Earhart flew her Lockheed Electra around the world's equator — the longest possible circumnavigation route. She completed 22,000 miles before disappearing with only 7,000 miles remaining.

Charles Lindbergh made the first solo transatlantic flight in 1927. Earhart was the first WOMAN to do so — in 1932, flying from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland in 14 hours 56 minutes. She also set the record for fastest transatlantic solo flight at that time.
challenge.instruction: Amelia Earhart was the first person to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean. The answer travels in cipher — turn the wheel until it reads.
Earhart communicated with ground crew using radio codes. Guess the 6-letter word that describes her mission across the Atlantic.
challenge.fact: Amelia Earhart flew solo across the Atlantic on 20 May 1932 in 14 h 56 min — fighting ice on her wings, a broken altimeter, and a flame leaking from her exhaust manifold.
